title: EAT SMART Teen Study
official: Effects of Application-based Eating Awareness Training on Disordered Eating in Youth With Obesity: The EAT SMART Teen Study
summary:
The goal of this controlled trial is to assess the feasability and efficacy of a 12-week mindfulness-based intervention (MBI) in adolescents living with obesity. The study will include youth ages 12 to 17 who are waitlisted at the Centre for Healthy Active Living (CHAL) at the Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario (CHEO).

We hypothesize that the MB-EAT Teen intervention will demonstrate good feasibility and usability among adolescents living with obesity. We also expect that, compared with the EAT SMART Teen psychoeducation program, MB-EAT Teen may lead to greater improvements in disordered eating behaviours, food-related self-regulation, mindfulness, emotional well-being, body image, and health-related quality of life.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Have access to a mobile/tablet device with internet access
* Are aged 12-17 years
* Are waitlisted or have recently been waitlisted for treatment at CHAL at CHEO
* Must sign and date the informed consent form, or provide assent and have a Substitute Decision Maker (SDM) provide informed consent
* Have the ability to complete the study in English

Exclusion Criteria:

* Are currently enrolled in a weight management program
* Have previously been diagnosed with Bulimia Nervosa, purging subtype
* Have previously been diagnosed with a condition that may impair their participation (e.g. cognition and/or neurodevelopment, particularly Fetal Alcohol Syndrome, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Down Syndrome, Prader- Willi Syndrome, Fragile X Syndrome)
* Have previously been diagnosed with a neurodevelopmental disorder (e.g., ADHD) and symptoms are not controlled by medication
* Have been diagnosed with a concussion in the past 6-months
